question: kinda scared to ask but how do i drop a class

body.answer:
It’s okay to ask. If you’re in the add/drop period, you can drop the course online through Web Self Service; courses dropped by the last day of Add/Drop won’t appear on your transcript. [17]

During the 50% refund period, you can drop in Web Self Service or submit a 50% Drop Form to the Registrar. Check the academic calendar for the deadline. [17]

After the refund period, you can withdraw through Web Self Service. The course will show a “W” on your transcript, there’s no refund, and you can’t withdraw after the published deadline. [20]

Check the academic calendar for the dates: [https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/). Dropping or withdrawing can affect financial aid and other things, so it’s a good idea to seek advice from your instructor or academic advisor. [1]

**Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [31]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/quicklinks/academicpolicies#dropping-or-withdrawing-from-a-course1) [17](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/registrationinfo/) [20](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

It’s okay to ask. If you’re in the add/drop period, you can drop the course online through Web Self Service; courses dropped by the last day of Add/Drop won’t appear on your transcript. [17]

During the 50% refund period, you can drop in Web Self Service or submit a 50% Drop Form to the Registrar. Check the academic calendar for the deadline. [17]

After the refund period, you can withdraw through Web Self Service. The course will show a “W” on your transcript, there’s no refund, and you can’t withdraw after the published deadline. [20]

Check the academic calendar for the dates: [https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/). Dropping or withdrawing can affect financial aid and other things, so it’s a good idea to seek advice from your instructor or academic advisor. [1]

question: transferring in next fall, how do i send my transcripts

body.answer:
Have each college you attended send its official transcript directly to Admissions. It can be sent electronically to admissions@ramapo.edu or mailed to: Ramapo College of New Jersey, Attn: Admissions, 505 Ramapo Valley Road, Mahwah, NJ 07430. [2]

If you are currently enrolled in college courses when you apply, submit your final transcript before enrolling. [2] If you have attempted fewer than 45 college credits, you also need to submit an official high school transcript. [2][5]

For transcripts from outside the United States, submit a course-by-course evaluation from a current NACES member. [2]

**Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7300. Email: admissions@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [34]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/admission-requirements/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/faqs/) [34](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

Have each college you attended send its official transcript directly to Admissions. It can be sent electronically to admissions@ramapo.edu or mailed to: Ramapo College of New Jersey, Attn: Admissions, 505 Ramapo Valley Road, Mahwah, NJ 07430. [2]

If you are currently enrolled in college courses when you apply, submit your final transcript before enrolling. [2] If you have attempted fewer than 45 college credits, you also need to submit an official high school transcript. [2][5]

For transcripts from outside the United States, submit a course-by-course evaluation from a current NACES member. [2]

question: i failed my calc midterm and idk what to do

body.answer:
That's stressful, but one bad grade doesn't decide everything. Talking with your professor and an advisor soon can really help.

**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): What’s going on? Tell me a little about the situation, and I’ll help you figure out a next step.

A bad midterm doesn’t necessarily mean you’ve failed the course. If you need help with Calculus I, the STEM Center offers tutoring: 1-on-2 by appointment through Connect, Saturday 11:00 AM–12:00 PM with Olivia Pettinelli; 1-on-3 by appointment through Connect, Monday 9:00–10:00 AM with Eva Avagyan; Monday 4:00–5:00 PM with Catherine Bardzell; Tuesday 9:00–10:00 AM with Catherine Bardzell; Tuesday 12:00–1:00 PM with Mateo Roman; Wednesday 4:00–5:00 PM with Em Dickstein; Thursday 9:00–10:00 AM with Eva Avagyan; Friday 12:00–1:00 PM with Mateo Roman (Cancelled on 11/6). [21] The STEM Center is open to students to walk in and study. [23]

If you failed the class, you can retake up to two classes with an F. To have the F removed from your transcript, fill out a Repeat Fail (RF) form with the Center for Student Success. After you retake the class, the new grade appears on your transcript in addition to the RF, and your GPA will be adjusted accordingly. [27] I don’t have verified information about what your midterm score means for your final course grade; your instructor is most likely to help.

- **STEM Center**: Phone: Tutoring Coordinator – STEM Center (201) 684-7345; Director – STEM Center & Programs (201) 684-7774. Office: G-131. [30]
- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [30]

Sources: [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/stem-center/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/stem-center/) [27](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/faq/) [30](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: i cant afford my textbooks this semester is there any help

body.answer:
Money stress is really common, and you don't have to sort it out alone.

Yes. If you receive financial aid that will create a credit balance on your College account, you may be eligible for a Book Advance to buy textbooks and course-related materials and supplies before aid is disbursed. First, go to the Office of Financial Aid to check eligibility. If approved, the advance is posted to your account; purchases can be made at the Bookstore the following day. You need valid picture ID. EOF students must first see their EOF counselor. [15]

Ramapo also has the Follett Bookstore Scholarship for students with few financial resources to purchase books; bookstore staff select recipients. [26]

Contact Financial Aid or Scholarships for help with these options.

**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [29]

This office can help:
**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [30]

question: ive been really stressed n cant sleep, is there counseling

body.answer:
I'm sorry you're going through that. It's okay to not be okay, and you don't have to handle it alone.

Yes. Ramapo offers free, confidential individual counseling, in person or via telehealth. Counseling can help with stress, anxiety, and depressed moods. Call to schedule or stop by Counseling Services in D-216. [1][15]

Free, immediate teletherapy and wellness programming are also available through Uwill. [9]

For sleep, RISE Science is a sleep app available free to Ramapo students for four years upon signing up. [20]

**Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [32]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/uwill/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/faq/) [20](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-affairs/student-communications/mental-health-and-well-being-resources-fall-2026/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: tips for not being nervous during presentations?

body.answer:
**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages):
- Practice aloud a few times, ideally with one person listening, so the opening feels familiar.
- Take a slow breath before you begin, and pause between points; you don’t need to rush.
- Use brief notes with key ideas rather than memorizing every word.
- Look at a few friendly faces or just above the audience, and remember they’re there to hear your ideas—not judge every stumble.
- If you lose your place, pause, check your notes, and continue.

question: how do i save money as a broke college student

body.answer: **General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): Track spending for a week, then set a small weekly limit for flexible costs. Plan cheap meals, use a grocery list, and compare unit prices; cancel subscriptions you rarely use. Check for student discounts, borrow or buy used textbooks, and automate even a tiny savings transfer when money comes in. Avoid high-interest debt when you can, and focus first on essentials and bills.

Schedule of Talks: Laboring in Tropical Heat: Colonial Climatic Imaginaries, Thermal Inequality, and the Farmers’ Movement in India Professor Sanghamitra Padhy Heat on the planet has reached record-breaking levels, exceeding the thermal thresholds within which humans can safely adapt and function. In many parts of India, summer temperatures have risen above 104°F, with little diurnal variation, creating extremely dangerous conditions for outdoor laborers and communities without access to cooling. As Bharat Venkat (2023) argues, heat is not experienced uniformly: farm workers, in particular, endure extreme heat and humidity without legal protections such as access to shade, water breaks, or wage security—protections that ought to be recognized as fundamental human rights. Unlike hurricanes or cyclones, which are spectacular and visibly destructive, heat waves arrive invisibly and are, therefore, often illegible and considered difficult to regulate (Goodell 2023). Drawing on the thirteen-month-long Indian farmers’ movement and an analysis of two prominent grassroots publications (Trolley Times and the People’s Archive of Rural India), alongside colonial records, I examine how the embodied experiences of heat among farm laborers are rendered illegible by the state, and how farmers are made disposable in the pursuit of neoliberal agricultural policies. Building on James Scott’s framework of legibility and illegibility, I explore the farmers’ movement in India to trace the entanglement of climate and agrarian crisis, as well as the modes of resistance that challenge climatic injustice. Thermal inequality, I argue, is not a new phenomenon – it is historically rooted in colonial climatic imaginaries that portrayed native bodies as biologically acclimatized to heat and the tropics as “dangerous spaces” riddled with heat, humidity, and disease. Yet colonial accounts reveal that the British were deeply anxious about heat. European discomfort in tropical climates was hyper-visible – in sartorial choices, specific foods believed to ward off heat, epidemiological ideas about heat, and the stationing of officials at hill stations, among other practices — while native exposure was normalized and invisibilized. These racialized climatic imaginaries justified the use of native labor for economic and military interests while erasing imperial responsibility for the production of agrarian crises, which persists in neoliberal contexts as well. "text": "to any word limit or page limit. Avoid clichés – stay away from common terms or tired statements. Express an original thought. Hints to Improve Your Essay Your personal essay for different fellowships or different schools will vary because an effective personal statement addresses the definitive criteria of each specific organization. The personal essay is not a narrative résumé. Rather, it should tell a quick and meaningful story about you that the reader cannot glean from your transcripts and any relevant admission examination. A good personal essay conveys your individuality through concrete examples, details, and personal anecdotes. Be sure that the opening sentence and paragraph grab the reader and intrigue them to read further. Be honest about your achievements and strengths while staying modest and realistic about your weaknesses. Avoid being gimmicky, cute, arrogant, or self-deprecating. Try to be clear and graceful and focus more on your positive attributes. A Few Style Tips Find a thread that binds the paragraphs – for example, in your autobiographical narrative, start with your background and an experience/person that had a formative influence on your interest. You can then move to subsequent events/undertakings that honed your specific interest and discuss your academic growth. Then, discuss your future ambitions or long-term objectives. Finish with how the scholarship or graduate studies will contribute to your goals. Persuasive writing relies on strong verbs – nouns and adjectives are not as powerful. Verbs signify action and can show evidence of past performance rather than merely piling up nouns and adjectives. Use the active voice – the passive voice projects weakness. Choose precise words – use clear words and phrases rather than abstract ones. Don’t turn to the thesaurus in all instances. Avoid using etc. as it can show that you don’t know how to finish your sentence. Too many metaphors may confuse – ensure that your metaphors are precise. Avoid either putting more than one metaphor in a sentence or overextending the metaphor. Cut unnecessary preliminaries and inflated phrases – don’t explain what you are about to say, just say it. Phrases like, let me add, the fact that, on the whole, etc., should not be used. Use elegant sentence variations – be sure to vary your sentences. Vary structure: simple and complex, long and short, exclamations. Vary beginnings: start each sentence with a different noun, preposition, participle, or adjective. Vary sentence lengths: avoid overly long and complex sentences. What worked for Faulkner may not work you for you here. Vary words: do not use the same words if not used deliberately for effect. Use consistent verb tenses – if using background influences that are still with you, use present tense. For past experiences, use the past tense. You would be surprised what a difference this makes. No clichés – clichés are lazy expressions, sometimes. Do not use “very” – this is a crutch. The Cahill Career Development Center can help with your resume. Create a VMock account at vmock.com/rcnj, upload your resume for instant feedback, incorporate the feedback and upload again (10 uploads max per academic year), then upload a resume with a score of 85 or better to Handshake for review. You can also make an appointment with your Career Advisor to tailor your resume to your job or internship search. [10]

To book an appointment, create your Handshake profile and schedule with your career advisor. [18] The pages do not say whether you can just show up; I don’t have verified information about walk-ins. Contact the Cahill Career Development Center.

**Cahill Career Development Center**: Phone: Main Office (201) 684-7444; ASB Office (201) 684-7675. Email: careercenter@ramapo.edu. Main Office: C-209; ASB Office: ASB-513. [33]

Sources: [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/careercenter/vmock/) [18](https://www.ramapo.edu/careercenter/four-year-plan/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)
